subject.title: Org claim: vmware-aiops + vmware-monitor — @kingaiwork lookalikes impersonate @zw008 listings (same pattern as #2966/#3035)

question: After verifying the reported production IDs, should staff permanently delete the two orphaned @kingaiwork skill records and apply account-level enforcement for the repeated impersonation pattern?
rationale: This requires privileged destructive production access and a trust-and-safety decision; source inspection cannot safely determine record ownership, dependent cleanup, audit retention, or the appropriate account sanction.

options.title: Delete verified orphan records
options.body: Audit the IDs and dependencies, hard-delete only the two @kingaiwork records, restore scan/listing progress, and review the publisher account for coordinated abuse.

options.title: Rename and retain records
options.body: Move the disputed records to nonconflicting slugs while preserving audit evidence, then verify that no global slug lookup remains ambiguous.

options.title: Leave records hidden
options.body: Retain the current soft-hidden state, accepting that the demonstrated scan and publish failures remain unresolved.

recommendation.title: Delete verified orphan records
recommendation.body: Audit the IDs and dependencies, hard-delete only the two @kingaiwork records, restore scan/listing progress, and review the publisher account for coordinated abuse.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history spans the namespace-policy RFC, ClawScan integration, scan repair, deletion, and hard-delete lifecycle needed for this decision.
